lines:
## Goal

Ship a small set of **standard global skills bundled with Aworkit** that teach an agent how Aworkit itself works, so the agent can help build, extend, explain and analyse Aworkit. They must be available on a fresh profile with **no user setup**.

## Why this is needed

- Today an Aworkit user's agent knows nothing about Aworkit's own concepts, so it cannot reliably help author workflows, plugins or skills, or explain where a chat is stored.
- Codex and Claude ship built-in skills of this kind; **Aworkit ships none**. Verified: there is no `SKILL.md` anywhere in the repository and `bundledSkillDir` defaults to empty.
- Skills are the right mechanism: progressive disclosure means the agent pays almost nothing until a topic is relevant, and the description decides when it loads.

## Skills to author (one folder each: `SKILL.md` + optional `references/`)

1. **how Aworkit skills work** — `SKILL.md` format and frontmatter, discovery roots and precedence, model vs `/name` invocation, the invocation controls, and how to author and test a new skill.
2. **how Aworkit plugins work** — the three layers (skill = procedure, MCP tool = capability + configuration, plugin = installable package), the plugin folder, package/manifest layout, MCP transport (local and server), configuration and credentials, enable/trust, side-effect hints, and the removal/update semantics.
3. **how Aworkit workflows work** — the graph model and **every node type with its configuration keys**, validation, what freezes per Chat vs what is re-resolved each pass, and how to author, validate and save a workflow. Enough for the agent to help create and analyse graphs.
4. **how Aworkit stores chats** — local SQLite semantic history: stream/run/branch identity, semantic events, attempts, spans, checkpoints, deduplication and outbox rows, the disposable read-only projections, and portable sessions. Enough to answer "where is my chat stored?" and to inspect or debug history.

## Mechanism

- Wire a real **bundled skill folder shipped with the build** and point the existing `bundledSkillDir` default at it, so the skills appear with zero configuration. It is empty today.
- Bundled skills follow the app version: a release updates them. They never modify a user's own skills.
- Keep the existing precedence: bundled skills are scanned **last**, so project and user skills of the same name still win.

## Quality bar

- Each skill needs a **description that actually triggers** on the right request — the description is the only thing the agent sees before loading.
- Plain language; define jargon rather than assuming it.
- Content must be **true to the current build**, not aspirational — above all the node catalog and the storage schema.
- Guard against drift: the workflow skill's node list and the storage skill's record names must come from a single source of truth, with a test/CI check that fails when the code changes and the skill does not.
- Keep each body short and push detail into `references/` (progressive disclosure).

## Acceptance criteria

- On a fresh profile with no user configuration, all four skills are discovered and listed.
- Asking the agent to author a skill, author a plugin, author a workflow, or to say where chats are stored triggers the correct skill.
- The workflow skill enumerates **all** current node types and their configuration keys; a drift check fails if a node is added or removed without updating it.
- The chat-storage skill matches the real SQLite schema and the portable-session facts.
- Upgrading the app updates the bundled skills without touching user or project skills.
- A same-named project or user skill still takes precedence over the bundled one.
- No user-facing jargon without explanation.

## Relationship to other work

- Depends on #172 for the plugin skill's content (the plugin/MCP shape).
- #172's "how to build a plugin" **agent skill** is authoring documentation for plugin developers; these bundled skills teach the agent how Aworkit works. Cross-reference them, do not duplicate content.
- Complements #176 (the see/install/manage surface for skills).

data.title: Ship bundled standard skills that teach an agent how Aworkit works (skills, plugins, workflows, chat storage)
